memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: Offer the second lamb at twilight, along with the same kind of grain offering and drink offering that you offer in the morning. This is a food offering, an aroma pleasing to the LORD. - Num 28:8 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
The evening offering mirrored the morning one exactly: the same lamb, the same grain, the same drink offering. Just as the day began with worship, so it was to close with worship. God's people were not to grow weary or careless as the day wore on. The evening sacrifice was as important as the morning one.

This speaks to the challenge of finishing well. It is often easy to begin the day with good intentions and devotion, but harder to end it with the same faithfulness. By evening we are tired, distracted, and ready to rest. Yet God called His people to worship Him at twilight as faithfully as at dawn. Devotion was to bracket the whole day.

The particular offering, of course, belonged to the old covenant and is fulfilled in Christ. But the lesson of steady faithfulness endures. God is worthy of our worship not only when we are fresh and eager, but also when we are weary and the day has drained us. Ending the day with Him keeps our hearts anchored.

In Christ, we have one who never grows weary and whose faithfulness never fades from morning to evening (Heb 13:8). His sacrifice covers us through every hour. Let the evening offering remind you to close each day turned toward the Lord, resting in the finished work of Jesus and giving Him the thanks of a full day lived in His presence.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
1. Do you finish your days as faithfully as you begin them?
2. How can you close each day turned toward the Lord?
3. What does it mean that Christ's faithfulness never fades?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Lord, help me to worship You not only at the fresh start of the day but also at its weary close. Anchor my heart in Christ from morning to evening, that I may finish each day faithfully. Amen.
